occasions.moment: the 4pm dip at a desk — hungry, flagging, two hours from dinner
occasions.competes_with: biscuits from the office jar, a chocolate bar, samosa/vada from the canteen, chai, a banana, or skipping it entirely
occasions.decided_by: speed, taste, what is within arm's reach, mild guilt
occasions.channel: office pantry, vending machine, the desk drawer stocked on Blinkit

occasions.moment: 11pm, scrolling in bed, wants something sweet
occasions.competes_with: chocolate, ice cream, leftover mithai, biscuits, nothing
occasions.decided_by: craving, what is in the fridge, 10-minute delivery
occasions.channel: Blinkit / Zepto / Instamart, the kitchen cupboard

occasions.moment: straight after the gym, 45 minutes before a proper meal
occasions.competes_with: a whey shake, eggs, a banana, dal-chawal at home, nothing
occasions.decided_by: protein per serving, habit, what the trainer said
occasions.channel: gym counter, HealthKart, Amazon, the gym bag

occasions.moment: leaving the house late, will not sit down to eat
occasions.competes_with: toast, poha, cereal, a bought sandwich, coffee alone, skipping
occasions.decided_by: one hand, no crumbs, keeps until 11am
occasions.channel: kitchen counter, the metro station kiosk, monthly grocery order

occasions.moment: a weekend or a bad day — wants a treat but not to feel bad about it
occasions.competes_with: dark chocolate, a 'healthy' dessert, regular chocolate anyway, fruit
occasions.decided_by: permission — whether it reads as a treat or as a compromise
occasions.channel: quick commerce, the supermarket aisle, a cafe

occasions.moment: airport, long drive, or a two-hour commute with no real meal in sight
occasions.competes_with: airport sandwich, chips, nuts, a Snickers at the counter, nothing
occasions.decided_by: portability, shelf life, what the counter is selling
occasions.channel: airport store, highway stop, petrol pump, packed from home

occasions.moment: a standing daily habit someone has decided to keep
occasions.competes_with: a powder, gummies, a multivitamin, real food, nothing
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it is working, cost per day
occasions.channel: Amazon subscribe, HealthKart, the pharmacy, D2C

occasions.moment: the monthly or weekly shop — buying for other people as well as themselves
occasions.competes_with: biscuit packs, namkeen, cereal, whatever the kids will eat
occasions.decided_by: price per unit, family acceptance, keeps in the cupboard

everyday_alternatives: Cadbury Dairy Milk — ₹10 to ₹100 depending on size; the default sweet thing
Snickers — ~₹40 for 50g; the 'it's basically food' bar at the counter
Britannia Good Day, Marie Gold, 50-50, Bourbon — ₹10-₹40 biscuit packs
Parle-G — ₹5-₹10; the floor of the category
Sunfeast Dark Fantasy — ~₹30; the indulgent biscuit
Lay's / Kurkure / Bingo — ₹20 chips and namkeen
Haldiram's namkeen — ₹20-₹50 packs, and the household tin
Amul / Kwality Walls ice cream — ₹40-₹80 for the late-night version
canteen samosa, vada pav, or chai — ₹10-₹25, hot and immediate
a banana or an apple from the fruit cart — ₹10-₹20
leftover mithai in the fridge after any festival
nothing at all — waiting it out until the next meal

raw.label: loyalist_four_oclock_biscuit_tin
raw.l1_context: Afternoon tea has been made in the same house at the same hour for twenty years; the tin beside the stove is part of it.
raw.l2_category: Buys the ₹40 Marie Gold pack and a ₹10 Parle-G every kirana trip, four or five times a week, on the running tab.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows which biscuit softens in tea and which crumbles. Does NOT know what a protein bar costs or where it is sold; does NOT know the word maltodextrin or that labels are read back-to-front by anyone.
raw.l4_stance: Wants tea to have something with it, cheap and familiar. Rejects anything that has to be ordered on a phone or explained to her.
raw.l5_behavior: Sent the neighbour's boy down for Marie Gold last week when the tin ran out before the afternoon tea.

bundles.occupation_hint: runs the house — cooking twice a day, the water drums, and her mother-in-law's medicines
bundles.household_hint: husband works on a contract in Bhubaneswar and comes home two weekends a month; four children, the youngest still in college

bundles.occupation_hint: sorts and packs mustard sacks at a small oil-pressing unit on the bypass, paid by the sack
bundles.household_hint: widowed nine years ago; lives with her married son, his wife and their two small children

bundles.occupation_hint: sits at the counter of the family's cycle-and-spares shop all afternoon and takes no salary from it
bundles.household_hint: three children; the eldest daughter married out last year and lives two villages away

raw.label: switcher_shrunk_pack_grudge
raw.l1_context: Counted the biscuits in the afternoon pack and found two fewer than she remembered, twice in one year. Has been moving around since.
raw.l2_category: Buys whatever the shop has in the biggest pack for the price; switched to loose biscuits from the sweet-shop jar for tea some weeks.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the pack weight printed on the front and that the bag is half air. Does NOT know that protein bars are sold as boxes of eight; does NOT know what 'clean label' is supposed to mean.
raw.l4_stance: Wants the same food for the same coin. Rejects any pack that puffs itself up, and rejects paying more to be told it is healthier.
raw.l5_behavior: Stopped buying the ₹35 Lay's pack for the house and started buying loose sev by weight from the kirana instead.

bundles.occupation_hint: stitches blouse pieces taken in from a tailor down the lane, paid per piece
bundles.household_hint: four children; her husband has been out of work since the flour mill closed and helps her cut cloth

bundles.occupation_hint: works other people's kitchens in the mornings — three houses, cooking and washing up
bundles.household_hint: husband died six years ago; her unmarried younger son sleeps at home and looks for work at the transport yard

bundles.occupation_hint: clerk in the records room of a co-operative bank branch, files loan papers all day
bundles.household_hint: two daughters, one in class 12; her mother lives with them and cannot get down the stairs alone

raw.label: upgrader_report_number_shifted
raw.l1_context: A sugar reading on last year's check-up report changed what is allowed at teatime; the doctor said cut the sweet, not the tea.
raw.l2_category: Now buys Bournville or roasted chana for the 4pm tea instead of the cream biscuit; orders on the ten-minute app twice a month.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows dark chocolate is 'less sweet' and that her reading came down. Does NOT know how much protein she should eat in a day; does NOT know the difference between whey and plant protein.
raw.l4_stance: Wants a small afternoon thing that will not show on the next report. Rejects the pastel powder pouches her niece pushes — that is not food.
raw.l5_behavior: Kept a Bournville in the steel dabba on the shelf and broke two squares with her tea last Sunday.

raw.label: aspirant_daughter_sent_bar
raw.l1_context: A daughter working in a city sent a box home and said take one at teatime instead of the biscuits. It sat in the cupboard, then got tried.
raw.l2_category: Has never bought one herself; eats what is sent or brought. Buys biscuits and namkeen at the kirana every week otherwise.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows her daughter says it has protein and is 'better for the joints'. Does NOT know the price of the box; does NOT know which shop or app would even have it in her town.
raw.l4_stance: Wants what the children in cities take, if it truly helps the knees. Rejects being told to give up the evening tea biscuit altogether.
raw.l5_behavior: Ate one of the RiteBite bars from the courier box with her afternoon tea and told her daughter it was chewy but fine.

raw.label: skeptic_ghee_dal_rice
raw.l1_context: Bought a jar of something a chemist recommended for weakness years ago, finished half of it, felt nothing, and never bought a packet health thing again.
raw.l2_category: Makes her own afternoon thing — chivda, roasted peanuts, leftover roti with ghee. Buys packaged snacks only when guests come.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows ghee, jaggery and dal keep a body going and that packet food goes stale differently. Does NOT know what 20g protein means; does NOT know any of the health-food brand names.
raw.l4_stance: Wants food cooked in her own kitchen. Rejects paying eighty rupees for one small wrapped bar — that is a day's vegetables.
raw.l5_behavior: Roasted a batch of chana and poha on Sunday and kept it in the steel dabba for the week's four o'clock tea.
